name: Assling
kurzbeschreibung: Sprawling rural community in the Pustertal with traditional hamlets and the popular Badesee.
beschreibung:
Overview

Assling is a sun-drenched municipality in East Tyrol, located in the Lienz district along the scenic plateau overlooking the Puster and Drau valleys. The territory spans from the valley floor in Thal at approximately 800 meters to the main center of Unterassling at 1,128 meters, reaching up to the craggy summits of the Villgraten Mountains exceeding 2,700 meters. Around 1,800 residents live spread across 18 hamlets and farming communities along the famed Puster Valley Sun Terrace. Characterized by authentic alpine farming, unspoiled natural scenery, and open panoramic views of the Lienzer Dolomites, Assling is an ideal sanctuary for nature enthusiasts and families.

History

Human settlement on this fertile terrace dates back to early medieval times. The village was first recorded around 1030 as Aznich in an episcopal exchange charter. Linguists trace the name back to the Old Slavic asenьnikь, meaning ash forest, reflecting the early presence of Carantanian Slavs before Bavarian settlers arrived. In the Middle Ages, Assling belonged to the County of Görz and fell to the Habsburgs and Tyrol around 1500 upon the extinction of the Görz line. Following a devastating fire in 1723, the Baroque parish church of the Holy Trinity in Unterassling was built by master builder Nikolaus Ströner. Another cultural gem is the church of St. Justina, perched high on a rock outcrop, built around 1500, featuring a Late Gothic winged altar and a remarkable fresco of Saint Christopher bearing an Arabic Kufic inscription.

How to Get There

By car, Assling is reached from Lienz via the Drautal federal highway B100 heading towards Sillian in about 15 minutes. At Thal, the well-maintained Pustertaler Sonnenstraße L356 winds up the terrace in panoramic switchbacks towards Unterassling. From Innsbruck or South Tyrol, access is via the Pustertal road through Innichen and Sillian. Train travelers take the Drau Valley Railway to Thal in Osttirol station or Mittewald an der Drau. Regional VVT bus routes connect the valley railway stops with the high-altitude hamlets.

Tips

A top highlight for families is the Assling Wildlife Park at 1,200 meters altitude, spanning 80,000 square meters and housing over 35 indigenous alpine wildlife species including ibex, chamois, lynx, and marmots. Adjacent to the park, the Fun-Alpin summer toboggan run delivers exciting downhill fun. In the valley near Thal, the Vitalpinum wellness park and mountain pine oil distillery Unterweger features an open-air sensory garden and barefoot trail. Cyclists enjoy the famous Drau Cycle Path R1 along the river, while hikers ascend to the Compedal alpine hut and Mount Rauchkofel. Winter offers natural tobogganing and tranquil ski touring throughout the Villgraten Mountains.
